title: Facial Pain
diagnosis: Trigeminal neuralgia or other neuropathic facial pain (due to facial pain presentation)
correct_orders: Obtain a detailed history, focusing on the onset, duration, and characteristics of the pain
Perform a neurological examination, including cranial nerve evaluation
Order MRI or CT with contrast to evaluate for any structural lesions in the trigeminal nerve region
Consider referral to a neurologist or neurosurgeon for further evaluation and management if MRI/CT reveals abnormalities
Initiate pain management as needed, such as carbamazepine or gabapentin, while awaiting specialist consultation
should_avoid: Immediate surgical intervention without proper diagnostic workup

rationale.Immediate surgical intervention without: Risk of unnecessary invasive procedure, potential complications, and suboptimal management
rationale.Oxygen: To provide immediate oxygen support for the patient experiencing facial pain.
rationale.IV access x2: To establish large-bore IV access in preparation for fluid resuscitation and administration of medications.

physical_exam: Facial Pain — exam tailored to chief complaint on arrival.
Soft, non-distended, no focal peritoneal signs on initial exam.
Alert and oriented unless perfusion or metabolic derangement present.
Warm skin with fever; no purpura on initial survey.
